name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Routing *all* zero-speech videos to curation with a "Needs Manual Review" label shifts 30% of uploads to a team that isn’t scaled for it—curation’s 30-second review adds hours weekly, and their core job is high-value content, not triage. Instead, task ingestion to route *only* videos under 10 seconds with zero speech to curation; longer silent videos (sign language, narrated slides) go to transcript with a "Silent but valid" flag. Settle this with a pilot: run the 10-second rule for a week, measure curation load and misclassification rates, then decide.

name: Reel
text: Task the ingestion team to route **all** zero-speech videos to curation with a clear label: "Needs Manual Review." This keeps sign-language, narrated slides, and rare edge cases out of the transcript pipeline while avoiding misclassification risks. The trade-off is shifting 30% of silent uploads to curation’s 30-second review, but it’s the safest way to avoid rejecting legitimate content or drowning the transcript team in noise.

name: Sift
text: Task the ingestion team to route *all* zero-speech videos to curation—this guarantees sign-language and narrated slides survive, but it dumps 30% of uploads on curation, which isn’t staffed for that load. Instead, task the ingestion team to run a lightweight 5-second speech classifier: if zero speech, route to curation *only* if the video is under 10 seconds; longer silent videos bypass curation and go straight to transcript. Settle it with a week-long pilot measuring curation load and misclassification rates.

name: Scope
text: Task the ingestion team to route **all** zero-speech videos to curation with a clear label: "Needs Manual Review." This guarantees sign-language, narrated slides, and edge cases never waste transcript time while keeping the pipeline honest—no risky shortcuts. The trade-off is shifting 30% of silent uploads to curation, but their 30-second review is still cheaper than misclassifying ASMR or music as "sign language." Curation’s bottleneck is real, but it’s the only team with the judgment to handle the edge cases.
